title: Exact analytical spectrum, eigenstates, and quantum geometry of the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model
abstract: Quantum geometry has emerged as a guiding principle across atomic and condensed-matter physics, shaping the topological responses of Bloch bands and the stability of the correlated phases they host. Beyond two-band models, however, closed-form expressions for both the spectrum and the quantum geometry are rare. Here we provide such expressions for a paradigmatic four-band model that has recently been realized experimentally with ultracold atoms, photons and in superconducting circuits: the Harper-Hofstadter model at quarter flux, describing charged particles on a two-dimensional square lattice subjected to a uniform magnetic field. We achieve this by first showing that the model possesses a sublattice symmetry, which renders its Bloch Hamiltonian anti-block-diagonal allowing us to derive the spectrum and the eigenstates analytically. From that we also obtain closed-form expressions for the full quantum geometric tensor (QGT), including both the Berry curvature and the quantum metric, for all the bands of the model. For this purpose we first derive a general expression for the QGT for sublattice-symmetric systems in terms of contributions from the individual sublattice sectors. Finally, we evaluate fractional-Chern-insulator stability criteria analytically and quantify the lowest band of the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model to be a nearly ideal Chern band.
summary: This paper provides an exact analytical solution for the spectrum and quantum geometry of the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model. By exploiting sublattice symmetry, the authors derive closed-form expressions for the energy bands and the full Quantum Geometric Tensor. The results confirm the model's topological nature, showing the lowest band is nearly an ideal Chern insulator, which is highly relevant for experimental realization using ultracold atoms.
main_problem: To derive exact analytical expressions for the spectrum, eigenstates, and quantum geometry of the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model.
main_result: The model is solved analytically by exploiting sublattice symmetry, revealing that the lowest band is nearly an ideal Chern band with a calculated Chern number of -1.
method: The analysis uses the sublattice symmetry to block-diagonalize the Bloch Hamiltonian, allowing for the analytical derivation of the spectrum via singular value decomposition and the calculation of the full Quantum Geometric Tensor (QGT).
model_or_system: The system is the Harper-Hofstadter model, describing charged particles on a 2D square lattice subjected to a uniform magnetic field at quarter flux ($\alpha=1/4$). The model is realized in platforms like ultracold atoms and superconducting circuits.
key_observables: Full Quantum Geometric Tensor (QGT), Berry curvature, quantum metric, Chern numbers ($C_n$), and various integrated stability defects (e.g., $	ext{THH}$).
important_parameters: Quarter flux ($\alpha=1/4$), lattice geometry (2D square lattice), and the magnetic field strength.
main_assumptions: The analytical solution hinges on the preservation of sublattice symmetry in the symmetric $2 	imes 2$ Magnetic Unit Cell (MUC) in quasimomentum space.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy spectrum along high-symmetry paths and across the full Brillouin zone, confirming the analytical results for the four bands.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model and the symmetry enabling the analytical solution. It then derives the spectrum and eigenstates, followed by the calculation of the QGT. Finally, it evaluates global stability criteria for hosting Fractional Chern Insulators (FCIs).
why_interesting: The explicit analytical solution for the QGT and the quantification of topological stability defects provide powerful, exact benchmarks for understanding topological phases in lattice models relevant to AMO experiments.
